case_name: R.R. Gopal @ Nakeeran Gopal v Union of India and Others
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows:
On 22.4.2003, this petition under Article 32 of the Constitution was filed by the petitioner seeking the following reliefs:
Although this notification is dated 24.12.2002, challenge to the constitutional validity of this notification independently of the validity of the Act itself, was not raised in the petition.

The same issue as to the constitutional validity of the Prevention of Terrorist Activities Act, 2002 (POTA) was being examined by this Court in Writ Petition No.389 of 2002, People's Union for Civil Liberties and Anr. vs. Union of India having gone into the issue in very many details, upheld the vires of the Act.

On 24.12.2002, G.O.Ms. No.1262 Home was issued by the State of Tamil Nadu whereby the State Government specified the whole of the State of Tamil Nadu as notified area for the purpose of Section 4 of the said Act.
issues: The constitutional validity of a notification issued under the Act is independent of the issue as to the constitutional validity of the Act itself.
The prayer for amendment is refused, but reserving liberty to the petitioner to raise the same issue by filing a petition before the High Court if so advised.
respondent_arguments: Heard the learned senior counsel for the parties.

The learned senior counsel for the respondent-State of Tamil Nadu raises a preliminary objection to the maintainability of this writ petition submitting that the same does not deserve now to receive consideration by this Court.
court_reasoning: So far as the principal reliefs prayed for in the writ petition are concerned, they do not survive for adjudication on merits in view of the decision of this Court dated 16th December,2003 in Writ Petition No.389/2002 People's Union for Civil Liberties and Anr. vs. Union of India 2004 Indlaw SC 62.
The petition, therefore, does not survive for adjudication.
However, now by way of amendment in the main petition, the petitioner seeks to put in issue the constitutional validity of a State notification issued under the Central legislation.
holding: Though the petition stands disposed of, the interim order dated 16.6.2003, passed by this Court shall continue to remain in operation for a period of six weeks from today.
cases_cited: Nakeeran Gopal v Union of India
